key_insight: The paper introduces multiagent debate protocols that transform and aggregate individual confidence signals into one system-level confidence, improving discriminative reliability without sacrificing answer correctness.
engineering_relevance: This enables NLP systems to expose a single calibrated confidence score for downstream routing, oversight, and decision-making in multiagent pipelines.
method: Normalize raw confidence signals so outputs from different agents/models become comparable.
Combine transformed confidences using soft voting or a proposed Bayesian fusion scheme.
Compare sequence-probability and self-report estimators with parametric and non-parametric calibration across debate setups.
evidence_signal: Across five benchmarks and four task types, using six homogeneous and heterogeneous agent pairs per benchmark, the proposed aggregation yields higher AUARC than single-agent and standard debate baselines while keeping F1 stable.
watch_item: Aggregated confidence depends on the quality of calibration and cross-model comparability, so mismatched estimators or poorly calibrated agents can weaken the reliability of the final score.
paper_title: Multiagent Protocols with Aggregated Confidence Signals
